solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Diamond? You won't get a bang from it

definitions.text: You won't get a bang from it

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a glittering gem

blocks.clueFragment: You won't get a bang from it
blocks.note: second meaning: a hand-held firework that fizzes and glitters but never explodes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the slang sense of the gem; the second half describes the quiet garden firework waved on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is jocularly called a sparkler, and the firework of that name burns with glittering sparks rather than exploding.

clue.text: Right canny dude hit the sack

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about and out of shape, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrewd fellow decides it is time to go to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit the sack' reads as an idiom for going to bed, but 'hit' is the shuffle signal and 'the sack' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the sack means losing your job, and being made redundant is the formal British term for that dismissal.

clue.text: All that's left of European political community

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a state is an organised political community under one government

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark about what remains of the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a political lament, but 'All that's left' is a definition: what someone leaves behind at death.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is the whole of the property and money remaining to be passed on after they die.

clue.text: Buzz, getting behind, becomes aggressive

blocks.note: a kick is a thrill or buzz, as in 'get a kick out of it'
ass is American slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Someone high on excitement, falling behind in a race, turns combative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word telling you where to put something, but it is just a noun for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Kick-ass is informal for forceful, combative and vigorously assertive, describing a pugnacious attitude.

clue.text: Unemotional Clinton not turned away by one state

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
something sent away is no longer present, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then read backwards
the Roman numeral for one
Cal is a short form for California

explanation.surface: Coldly, a Clinton is not dismissed by voters in one particular state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not turned away' reads as 'not rejected', but it splits: the reversed word is taken out of the surname. Cal is the familiar abbreviation for California.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinical behaviour is detached and efficient, coolly lacking any warmth or feeling.

clue.text: Ohio Republican bill taken up – it's a killer

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking something up lifts it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: O is the postal abbreviation for Ohio
R is the abbreviation for Republican
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A Republican bill from Ohio is passed, and it will be deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: A bill sounds legislative here, but it is an account, abbreviated AC; flipped upward it becomes CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is popularly called the killer whale, a large black and white predator of the oceans.

clue.text: Press's other version involving "X"

indicators.note: a new version is a different rendering, so the letters come out rearranged
to involve is to take in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: OTHER rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper's alternative account of events at the social network X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers, but it is a verb; the 's stands for 'is' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge someone strongly to act, which is what pressing them means.

clue.text: Having gone downhill, it's fun getting pear-shaped, smarmy kiss

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: to be shaped is to be moulded into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
smarmy suggests something slick and greasy, so the letters slide into a new order

blocks.note: PEAR rearranged
KISS rearranged

explanation.surface: Things have gone downhill and pear-shaped, ending in an oily, unwelcome kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone downhill' and 'pear-shaped' both suggest things going wrong, but downhill is literal skiing, and 'pear-shaped' splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising and partying in a resort after a day's skiing on the slopes.

clue.text: Ensnare with a kiss and glamrock wear?

blocks.note: to lure is to entice or trap
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Seducing someone with a kiss while dressed in 1970s glitter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: glam rock stars wore shiny metallic costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurex is a trademarked yarn woven with metallic thread, typical of glittery 1970s stage costumes.

clue.text: (& 25/20ac.) One reversal unduly mismanaged – poor handler of vaccine acquisition

indicators.note: something mismanaged is bungled and thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, all seventeen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A policy U-turn was badly handled by the official who botched buying vaccines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversal' tempts you to turn something round, but it is only fodder. Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission president, was blamed for the EU's slow 2021 Covid vaccine purchasing.
explanation.definitionFit: As head of the European Commission she oversaw its widely criticised, sluggish procurement of Covid vaccines early in 2021.

clue.text: (& 13ac.) Joey to make love? It won't do anyone justice

blocks.note: a joey is a baby kangaroo, so it leads to the animal
in the old sense, to make love is to woo or court

explanation.surface: Someone called Joey is told to make love, followed by a verdict that it is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Joey looks like a man's name; it is the Australian word for a young kangaroo. 'Make love' here is the old-fashioned sense of wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo court is an unofficial, biased tribunal that ignores proper legal process, so nobody gets fair treatment.

clue.text: Joy's end wobbled aboard schooner?

indicators.note: something wobbled is shaken unsteadily, so the letters lose their order
to be aboard is to be inside a vessel, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a schooner is a tall glass for sherry or beer
END rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Joy ended her voyage seasick on a rocking sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The schooner is not a boat but a drinking glass, hence the question mark; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladness is a plain synonym for joy: the state of being happy and pleased.

clue.text: see 11ac.
International body with cash remaining – Germany's disturbed

blocks.note: the United Nations
the balance is the money left in an account
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A world organisation with money to spare finds Germany upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' reads as Germany being troubled, but it is the definition in its mental-health sense; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mentally unbalanced is unstable or deranged, which is what disturbed means in this sense.

clue.text: Old person looking like a scrotum

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang noun for an elderly person
second meaning: an adjective for creased, furrowed skin

explanation.walkthrough: A typically rude Private Eye clue: the same word is a slangy British noun for a pensioner and an ordinary adjective for creased skin.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang an elderly person is a wrinkly, and anything covered in creases or furrows is wrinkly.

clue.text: "Only had a potty!" as the sailor cried

definitions.note: the definition is the cry itself, introduced by 'as'

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go haywire into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor complains that the only toilet available was a child's potty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like a chamber pot completing the quotation, but it is the crazy sense that signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Land ahoy is the traditional shout from a ship's lookout on first sighting the shore.

clue.text: Cry "too much fat!"

blocks.note: first meaning: to weep noisily
second meaning: excess body fat, as on a whale

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like someone crying out about fatty food; 'Cry' is a verb sense and the rest a noun sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to sob tearfully, and blubber is also the thick layer of fat on whales, or on an overweight person.

clue.text: A plea to "put away" during penetration

indicators.note: something happening during another event falls within it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: an entry is a way in, a penetration
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A request to stow something during a break-in, with a ruder undertone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests jailing or tidying, but here it means eating heartily.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or appeal, the same thing as a plea.

clue.text: Public record shows reluctant prince's son claiming victory

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: Prince Harry, who stepped back from royal duties, has a son named Archie
V for victory

explanation.surface: Official files reveal a royal heir boasting of a win.
explanation.walkthrough: The reluctant prince is Prince Harry, who quit royal life; his son is Archie.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical documents kept as a record, often held by public bodies.

clue.text: see 10ac.
'Flaky liberal' Starmer ultimately absent and bearing responsibility

indicators.note: something flaky crumbles and falls apart, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is wanted
what is absent is missing, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the Labour leader's name

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer, branded a wishy-washy liberal, is missing but still to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from LIBERAL, then rearrange the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being liable means being legally answerable or accountable for something, which is to carry responsibility.

clue.text: Euro's let off, that's decided

indicators.note: food that is off has gone bad, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The European currency is spared, and the matter is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' reads as a pardon; 'off' alone is the signal and the apostrophe's S is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A resolute person is firm and determined, just as a decided one has made up their mind firmly.

clue.text: Herb holds one against Lily

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: sage is a culinary herb
V, short for versus, means against
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone named Herb harbours a grudge against someone named Lily.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb and Lily look like two people's names. Lily Savage was the drag persona of the late British comedian Paul O'Grady.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Lily Savage, the brash Liverpudlian drag character created and played on British television by Paul O'Grady.

clue.text: Withdraw whip as a violent consequence

blocks.note: to back off or back away is to withdraw
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: Taking away a party whip's privileges brings angry repercussions.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics withdrawing the whip expels an MP from their party, which makes the surface sound like Westminster news.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong adverse reaction provoked by some event, often hostile or forceful.

clue.text: Love god's fate: king's out

indicators.note: something out is no longer in, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: karma is destiny earned by one's actions
R, from Rex, is king

explanation.surface: The fate of a deity of love is sealed once the monarch is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'; remove R from KARMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Kama is the Hindu god of desire and erotic love, as in the title of the Kama Sutra.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Oblivion is attained by putting ring on member

blocks.note: an arm or leg is a member of the body
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Bliss is reached by sliding a ring onto a certain body part.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so the ring is placed after the member; 'member' carries the usual Private Eye innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo means being forgotten or neglected in an uncertain state, close to oblivion.

clue.text: Vetting foreign and English character sketch

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters appear in a new order

blocks.note: VETTING rearranged
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Screening foreign and English applicants by a short written profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character sketch' could suggest a drawing; it is a brief literary portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a short descriptive piece of writing that captures a person or scene briefly.
